items.stem: What does AppSheet use as the system of record for an app's data?

options.text: The connected data source such as Google Sheets or a database
options.rationale: Correct: AppSheet reads and writes to the connected source; it is not a separate datastore.

options.text: An internal AppSheet-only database that replaces the source
options.rationale: AppSheet does not replace the source; it operates on the connected data.

options.text: The user's device local storage only
options.rationale: Device storage is a cache, not the system of record.

options.text: A static export taken at build time
options.rationale: Data is live against the source, not a one-time export.

items.explanation: Correct: the connected data source is the system of record.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which column type links a row in one table to a row in another table?

options.rationale: Correct: a Ref column creates a relationship to another table's key.
Text stores free text, not a relationship.
Number stores numeric values, not relationships.
Enum restricts to a fixed value list, not a table link.

items.explanation: Correct: Ref columns model relationships between tables.

items.stem: Which TWO are valid ways to limit the rows a user can see or edit in an AppSheet app? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Apply a security filter on the table
options.rationale: Correct: security filters restrict which rows sync to the user.

options.text: Set column or table permissions by role
Rely only on hiding a view from the menu
options.rationale: Hiding a view is cosmetic and does not restrict data.

options.text: Change the thumbnail of the app
options.rationale: The thumbnail has no effect on access.

items.explanation: Correct: security filters and role permissions both limit access.
